segment_summary: একদিকে মানুষের গলা আর কাঠের ওয়ারের সঙ্গীত, অন্যদিকে মেশিনের অমানুষিক চিৎকার — কবিতা শব্দের এই যুদ্ধকে আঁকে।

segment_enrichment.angle: Framing the diesel sound not as a mere noise, but as a competing dialect—a syntax of pure function versus the grammar of song.
segment_enrichment.story_option: Setting: A stretch of river where only automated barges move; Desire: Gopal attempts to sing a familiar verse, knowing he will be drowned out by the repetitive thrumming; Obstacle: The sheer, indifferent velocity of the cargo.
segment_enrichment.subject_rotation: Focusing solely on the pollution residue—the specific color and texture of diesel runoff contrasting against the natural ochre of monsoon silt.
segment_enrichment.sensory_detail: The acrid, hot smell of spent fuel clinging to the damp river mist during early dawn runs.
segment_enrichment.research_question: What is the relationship between sound pollution and perceived spiritual quality in Bengali river culture?
segment_enrichment.structural_variant: An extended internal monologue where Gopal narrates the engine’s mechanical processes as if it were an alien language he is struggling to translate into human feeling.
segment_enrichment.variety_note: While previous chapters dealt with environmental/cultural friction through geography (Concrete Floodwalls, Muddy Banks), this chapter isolates the conflict entirely within the sonic spectrum—a confrontation of pure sound versus rhythm.
